item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract and has far better scope discipline, though it still should delegate to FilesService.Add and strengthen its tests before merge.","reasons":["B directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile, producing the required replayable buffered multipart body with field \"file\" and the supplied filename.","B preserves FilesService.Add, FilesOption behavior, and retry infrastructure, while A expressly violates the contract by adding association form fields and changing global request-body replay and ownership semantics.","A introduces NewFileWithFields and calls Raw.Do directly, adding prohibited machinery and duplicating Add's request/response behavior.","Both implementations duplicate Add rather than routing Upload through it, but B can be corrected cleanly by returning s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...). A's extra form-option design makes that correction broader and conflicts with explicit requirements."],"risks_a":["Adds WithFilesFormFields and association fields despite the explicit prohibition.","Changes Raw.Do globally so seekable bodies are replayed and no longer closed by the transport, altering compatibility and resource-ownership semantics outside the requested scope.","enableBodyReplay may leave a seeker at the wrong offset if SeekEnd fails after changing position because it only restores the original offset on successful SeekEnd calls that enter the branch; it also reuses one mutable seeker across body instances rather than creating independent readers/handles for retries, which is fragile if body lifecycles overlap or the transport accesses them unexpectedly. Its docs also promise broader retry behavior beyond the frozen Upload-only contract, increasing maintenance and API-semantics risk. Upload bypasses Add and duplicates option handling, Raw.Do invocation, response decoding, missing-data validation, and error flow. The Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a concretely streamed/non-recognized source, while source-reader failures are not tested."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, directly duplicating its request construction, response decoding, missing-data validation, and error behavior, contrary to the contract.","Validation combines empty filename and nil content into one generic error and occurs after applying options; while no request is made, separate validation would be clearer and less surprising if an option has behavior.","No tests cover validation or propagation of source-reader failures. The retry test hides the source reader's concrete type but never reads or verifies the multipart body on the retried request, so it proves the retry count rather than replayed content integrity. The changelog inaccurately describes *os.File as a non-seekable source, even though files implement io.Seeker; the relevant point is that NewFile buffers any io.Reader into a bytes.Reader."]}
